claim: Baarle-Nassau (Netherlands) and Baarle-Hertog (Belgium) together form 30 enclaves: 22 Belgian pieces in Dutch land and 8 Dutch pieces inside Belgian land. The Kadaster polygon of Baarle-Nassau has 9 parts: one main body with 22 holes (Belgian enclaves) plus 8 detached pieces; the Flemish polygon of Baarle-Hertog has 26 parts, of which 22 are the Belgian enclaves and 4 are parts of the municipality outside the Dutch polygon.

evidence.quote: TOTAL outer parts: 9 holes: 22
geometry MultiPolygon parts: 26 parts with holes: 3

evidence.locator: page text, first sentence of 'Samenwerking met Baarle-Hertog'
evidence.quote: vormen samen een internationale legpuzzel van 30 enclaves
evidence.translation: together form an international jigsaw puzzle of 30 enclaves

notes: Two agencies, two countries, two coordinate systems agree. '30' is the municipalities' own count (22 + 8); the Dutch main body is not counted. Popular sources give 16, 20, 21, 22, 24 (see myths M5). Hedge-free: 'thirty enclaves' is the official count.
method: Kadaster rings counted by method/count_enclaves_pdok.py; Flemish parts by method/count_enclaves_flanders.py

claim: The same 22 Belgian enclaves appear in both countries' official maps: each of the 22 holes in the Dutch municipal polygon matches one Belgian part by area (largest 165.24 ha vs 165.28 ha; every pair within 0.04 ha). The 1995 procès-verbal numbers them H1 to H22 (the text quoted by Franckx names 'l'enclave H 22').

evidence.quote: max area difference over the 22 matched pairs: 0.04 ha
BE parts not matched to any NL hole (ha): [467.7, 18.49, 14.54, 9.08]

evidence.locator: p. 345, quoting the 1995 proces-verbal, Moniteur belge 26 June 1996 p. 17567
evidence.quote: est décrit au procès-verbal comme l’enclave H 22
evidence.translation: is described in the procès-verbal as enclave H 22

notes: H-numbering H1-H22 as a full range is from tourism copy (S17) and Franckx's single H 22; the official text of the PV was not opened.

claim: Of the 8 Dutch pieces, 7 lie inside Belgian enclaves (6 in the largest Belgian enclave, 165 ha, and 1 in the second largest, 42 ha) and 1 lies in Belgian land away from any enclave (2.85 ha, Flemish polygon: a hole in a Belgian part). Franckx's 1998 count agrees: 22 Belgian enclaves, two of which contain seven Dutch enclaves, plus an eighth Dutch enclave south of the state border.

evidence.quote: Dutch parts inside a Belgian hole: 7 | not inside any hole: 1
BE parts with holes: 3 | total Dutch holes inside BE parts: 8
twenty-two little Belgian enclaves on Dutch territory, two o f which themselves contain seven Dutch enclaves

notes: Franckx names the eighth piece 'Vossenberg' (note 3). We did not verify that our 2.85 ha piece is Vossenberg: do not name it in a script.

claim: The enclave borders add up to about 35 km. Summing the ring lengths in the Kadaster data gives 35.2 km (22 Belgian enclaves 30.2 km plus 8 Dutch pieces 5.0 km). Franckx, reading the 1995 procès-verbal, gives 'a little bit more than 35 km' of frontier.

evidence.quote: sum of hole perimeters: 30.17 km; sum of detached Dutch part perimeters: 5.04 km
a little bit more than 35 km o f frontier had to be fïxed

notes: Say 'about 35 km'. Ring lengths in a generalised polygon are an approximation; the PV figure is the legal one (read via Franckx only).
method: Sum of Euclidean ring lengths in RD New (metres) of the 22 holes + the 8 detached parts, method/enclave_geometry_pdok.py

claim: The boundary treaty between the Netherlands and Belgium was signed at Maastricht on 8 August 1843 and the ratifications exchanged on 3 October 1843, when it entered into force.

evidence.quote: Date of conclusion 08-08-1843 Place of conclusion Maastricht Provisional application Entry into force 03-10-1843
De bepalingen van de Overeenkomst zijn op 3 oktober 1843 in werking getreden.
evidence.translation: The provisions of the Agreement entered into force on 3 October 1843.

notes: Name in French: 'Convention fixant les limites' (S04). The 1974 Tractatenblad heading is wrongly shortened '1 (1843) Nr. 1' in the scan header; ignore.

claim: The 1843 convention treated Baarle as a special case: Article 1 says the two Baarle communes, where 'the status quo is maintained' under Article 14 of the treaty of 5 November 1842, are shown on a special plan in four sheets at 1:10,000, with two detached sheets at 1:2,500 for the parts too small to show clearly.

evidence.quote: Un plan spécial, en quatre feuilles, comprenant le parcellaire tout entier de ces deux communes, est dressé à l'échelle du dix-millième
evidence.translation: A special plan in four sheets, covering the whole parcel map of these two communes, is drawn at a scale of one ten-thousandth

evidence.quote: le statu-quo est maintenu, en vertu de l'article quatorze du traité du cinq Novembre mil huit cent quarante deux
evidence.translation: the status quo is maintained, by virtue of Article 14 of the treaty of 5 November 1842

evidence.quote: four maps to a scale o f 1/10.000 and two o f a scale o f 1/2.500

notes: The enclaves are therefore not created by 1843; the treaty froze them as they stood.

claim: At Baarle the 1843 convention did not draw a line. Article 14 paragraph 5 says that on reaching the communes of Baarle-Nassau and Baarle-Duc 'the limit is interrupted' because it is impossible to set it between them without a break, given the 1842 status-quo clause; the division of the communes between the two kingdoms 'is the subject of a special work'. The line resumes at the next boundary marker (214 to 215 is the gap).

evidence.quote: la litime est interrompue, par suite de l'impossibilité de l'établir, entre ces deux communes, sans solution de continuité
evidence.translation: the limit is interrupted, owing to the impossibility of setting it, between these two communes, without a break

evidence.quote: is de grens afgebroken, ten gevolge van de onmogelijkheid om dezelve, tusschen deze beide gemeenten, op eene doorloopende wijze daar te stellen
evidence.translation: the border is broken off, owing to the impossibility of placing it continuously between these two municipalities

evidence.quote: ter hoogte van grenspaal 214
evidence.translation: at the height of border post 214

evidence.quote: marker 214 in the east, dividing the Belgian municipality of Poppel and the Dutch municipality o f Alphen, and marker 215 in the west

notes: The typo 'litime' is in the source. Marker numbers 214 and 215: 214 verified in S01, 215 only in S15 (S).

claim: Article 14 of the treaty of 5 November 1842 said: the status quo shall be maintained for the villages of Baarle-Nassau (Netherlands) and Baarle-Duc/Baarle-Hertog (Belgium) and for the roads that cross them.

evidence.quote: „Le statu-quo sera maintenu, tant à l'égard des villages de Baarle-Nassau (Pays-Bas) et Baarle-Duc (Belgique), que par rapport aux chemins qui les traversent.”
evidence.translation: The status quo shall be maintained, as regards the villages of Baarle-Nassau (Netherlands) and Baarle-Duc (Belgium) and the roads that cross them.

evidence.quote: Le statu quo sera maintenu, tant à l’égard des villages de Baar-le-Nassau (Pays-Bas) et Baar-le-Duc (Belgique)
Le statu quo sera maintenu tant à l'égard des villages de Baarle-Duc (Belgique) et Baarle-Nassau (Pays-Bas), que par rapport aux chemins qui les traversent.

notes: The 1842 treaty text itself was not opened (quoted by three later official/scholarly texts). The 1842 treaty is dated 5 Nov 1842 in S01 (Stb. 1843, 3).

claim: The Baarle border was completed in two documents long after 1843. On 26 April 1974 at Turnhout a proces-verbal fixed the whole Dutch-Belgian line round Baarle-Nassau 'with the exception of all the enclaves' of Baarle-Hertog inside Baarle-Nassau.

evidence.locator: treaty record 002268, data block and title
evidence.quote: Date of conclusion 26-04-1974 Place of conclusion Turnhout
with the exception of all the enclaves that form part of the municipality of Baarle-Hertog and are situated within the municipal boundaries of Baarle-Nassau
Op 26 april 1974 is te Turnhout ondertekend een Proces-Verbaal van afbakening van de Rijksgrens
evidence.translation: On 26 April 1974 a proces-verbal of delimitation of the state border was signed at Turnhout

notes: Belgian publication: Moniteur belge 5 March 1975 pp. 2575-2581 (via S15).

claim: The enclave borders were fixed last by a proces-verbal signed at Baarle on 31 October 1995 by a newly set-up Royal Boundary Commission; it was not a treaty. Franckx: 'Not by means o f an agreement, but simply, as in 1974, by means o f &procès-verbal based on the old border agreement o f 1843'. Published in the Moniteur belge of 26 June 1996, pp. 17565-17594 (29 pages).

evidence.quote: On October 31, 1995 a second, and final, procès-verbal was arrived at
Not by means o f an agreement, but simply, as in 1974, by means o f &procès-verbal based on the old border agreement o f 1843
signé à Baarle le 31 octobre 1995, October 31, 1995, Moniteur belge du 26 juin 1996, pp. 17565- 17594

notes: NOT spine until the Moniteur belge page is opened (ejustice returned HTTP 500; Dutch Tractatenblad 1995 page 403). The Dutch treaty database lists the 1974 report as a child of the 1843 treaty and lists no 1995 instrument (S02, S03): consistent with 'not a treaty' but only a weak negative. Say 'by a procès-verbal in 1995' only with hedge until verified.

claim: In the 1995 proces-verbal about 35 km of frontier were fixed by 960 turning points on 249 ha 55 a 25 ca of land, and, because of the cost and the buildings in the way, the commission did not apply the 1843 rules for placing border markers to this part of the border.

evidence.quote: In order to divide 249 ha 55 a 25 ca of land, a little bit more than 35 km o f frontier had to be fïxed and this by means of not less than 960 turning points
Because of this complexity, the members o f the 1994 Royal Boundary Commission 1994 Royal Boundary Commission decided not to apply the

notes: 960 points vs our 1,720 ring vertices: different counting, do not compare.

claim: In 1959 the International Court of Justice, by ten votes to four, found that sovereignty over two disputed plots (nos. 91 and 92) belonged to Belgium; the Court's summary notes the 1841 communal record gave them to Baarle-Nassau and the 1843 descriptive procès-verbal and map gave them to Baerle-Duc.

evidence.locator: icj.org résumé of the judgment of 20 June 1959 (node 103797)
evidence.quote: Par 10 voix contre 4, elle a indiqué que la souveraineté sur ces parcelles appartenait à la Belgique.
evidence.translation: By 10 votes to 4, it indicated that sovereignty over these plots belonged to Belgium.

evidence.quote: Case concerning Sovereignty over Certain Frontier Land (Belgium/The Netherlands), 1959 I.G.J. Reports 209

notes: Verifier must open the judgment PDF in a normal browser (blocked here). Judgment date 20 June 1959 is in the ICJ page titles ('Résumé de l'arrêt du 20 juin 1959') seen in search results and in S15 (1959). The pig-farmer / ten-houses story is 'tradition' (S15 note 5): not used.

claim: The 1959 judgment gave Belgium 14 ha 37 a 80 ca (about 14.4 hectares), and the 1995 settlement a further 23 a 32 ca, 1.6 % of that.

evidence.quote: the Belgian territory increased by 14 ha 37 a 80 ca
23 a 32 ca to be précisé, i.e. only a small fraction (1.6 % ) o f the territory gained in 1959

notes: Internal inconsistency in S15: the 1995 parcel 'De Withagen' is quoted as 26 a 32 ca (cadastre A 3789) but the gain as 23 a 32 ca. Not for a script.

claim: In 1892 Belgium and the Netherlands signed a convention (11 June 1892, plus a declaration of 21 December 1892) to end the Baarle puzzle by exchange: Belgium would give up the Baarle-Duc agglomeration (and part of Weelde heath); the Netherlands would give Belgium the hamlets of Castelré and Ulicoten, part of Baarle-Nassau.

evidence.locator: Expose des motifs, p. 3 (OCR; corrected reading)
evidence.quote: les Pays-Bas devant céder à la Belgique le hameau de Castelré et celui d'Ulicoten, qui font partie de la commune de Baarle-Nassau, et la Belgique abandonnant l'agglomération de Baarle-Duc et une partie du territoire de Weelde
evidence.translation: the Netherlands to cede to Belgium the hamlet of Castelré and that of Ulicoten, which are part of Baarle-Nassau, and Belgium giving up the agglomeration of Baarle-Duc and part of Weelde

evidence.quote: ONTWERPEN VAN WET tot goedkeuring der overeenkomst met België van 11 Juni 1892, tot regeling der grens tusschen Baarle-Hertog en Baarle-Nassau
evidence.translation: Bills to approve the agreement with Belgium of 11 June 1892 regulating the border between Baarle-Hertog and Baarle-Nassau

evidence.quote: Pas in 1892 werd in het Belgische parlement een wetsontwerp ingediend waarin werd voorgesteld Ulicoten en Castelré te ruilen voor Baarle-Hertog

notes: The exchange terms come from the Belgian memorandum (an interested party). S05 text is a bad OCR of a scan; the verifier must read the PDF page (document 197, pp. 2-3). The scan also mis-OCRs 1893 as 1895 and 8 August as '18 août'.

claim: The 1892 exchange was designed to be even on people: the Belgian memorandum counts 728 inhabitants in the territory Belgium would cede (1887 count) and 726 in the territory the Netherlands would cede.

evidence.locator: Expose des motifs, p. 4 (OCR; corrected reading)
evidence.quote: le territoire cédé par la Belgique compte 728 habitants et celui cédé par les Pays-Bas en compte 726
evidence.translation: the territory ceded by Belgium has 728 inhabitants and that ceded by the Netherlands has 726

notes: Single source, Belgian government, 'd'après les constatations faites en 1887'. Same memorandum: Belgium cedes 266 ha 54 a 71 ca of Baarle-Duc.

claim: The 1892 exchange never took effect in Belgium: the government bill approving it was deposited in the Chamber on 24 May 1893 and carries a 'date de caducité' (lapse date) of 19 September 1894, with no vote recorded.

evidence.quote: Date de dépôt 24/05/1893 ; Date de caducité 19/09/1894
evidence.translation: filed 24/05/1893; lapse date 19/09/1894

notes: WebFetch extraction (curl refused); verifier must re-open. Wortel (S16) says the bill 'werd afgewezen' (was rejected) after a protest from Baarle-Hertog and the Turnhout member; the Chamber record shows lapse, not a vote: see conflicts K3. Say 'lapsed', not 'rejected'.

The Dutch outcome is not established by a primary record in this run. Wortel says the Dutch parliament dealt with it only in writing and it was 'afgedaan' (closed) in 1897.

der additioneele verklaring van 21 December 1892
evidence.translation: of the additional declaration of 21 December 1892

evidence.quote: In het Nederlandse parlement kwam het voorstel niet verder dan een schriftelijke behandeling en het werd in 1897 afgedaan.
evidence.translation: In the Dutch parliament the proposal went no further than a written procedure and was closed in 1897.

notes: Do not narrate the Dutch outcome.

claim: The 1974 report marks parts of the border that cannot be seen on the ground with stakes, stones and iron pipes, including one invisible stretch 'between a house and a barn' marked with iron pipes.

evidence.translation: an invisible border between a house and a barn that is marked with iron pipes

notes: This stretch is outside the enclaves (Baarle-Nassau / Baarle-Hertog mainland border). Not a café, not an enclave.

claim: The Netherlands' Kadaster defines the building-use category 'bijeenkomstfunctie' (assembly use) as use 'for gathering of persons, for art, culture, religion, communication, childcare, serving consumptions for use on the spot and watching sport'; the building register lists cafes and restaurants under this heading, but also churches and canteens.

evidence.quote: voor het gebruik ter plaatse en het aanschouwen van sport.
evidence.translation: for use on the spot and watching sport

evidence.quote: het verstrekken van consumpties
evidence.translation: serving consumptions

notes: Used only to say what the building-register data can and cannot show.

claim: Building footprints in the Dutch building register (BAG) are cut by the national border line in the largest Belgian enclave: our overlay finds 41 in-use footprints properly crossed (10 of them with a registered use: 4 homes, 5 shops, 2 with assembly use, depending on the tolerance), but the result changes with the crossing tolerance (0.3 m vs none gave 59 and 21) and the register holds Dutch buildings only.

evidence.quote: in use AND with at least one registered verblijfsobject (a unit with a use): 10

notes: UNVERIFIED for narration. It shows that the line cuts through buildings, not which ones are cafes. A geodetic-grade check (and a Belgian building layer) would be needed.
method: method/buildings_on_border.py (proper crossing of footprint edges with the Kadaster H1 boundary ring; tolerance 0.3 m)

claim: No official record read in this run names a cafe (or any named business) through which the border runs. Official records name houses (the 1995 procès-verbal, via Franckx, 'a house divided in two by one of these lines'), a house and a barn (1974).
